regions.description: Every pixel in the nside=128 NESTED HEALPix domain. Required baseline region; every other region is a subset of this one.
Low Galactic latitude band |b| <= 10 deg, where stellar crowding and dust extinction are highest and where the candidate map's source-accumulation and exclusion logic is most stressed.
15 deg cone around the Galactic Center (l=0, b=0): highest stellar density and extinction in the sky, a critical stress test for both bias and coverage metrics.
15 deg cone around the Galactic anticenter (l=180, b=0): moderate stellar density along the plane but far from the bulge, useful as a plane-region contrast to galactic-center.
High Galactic latitude band |b| >= 60 deg, covering both Galactic poles: lowest stellar density and extinction, where absolute-bias tolerances are most sensitive to small systematic offsets.

Union of small fields around classic low-HI-column-density 'dark window' extragalactic survey fields (Lockman Hole, Extended Groth Strip, Chandra Deep Field South), chosen independently of this repository's map because they are the fields the diffuse-light literature already treats as having minimal foreground contamination.
regions.limitation: Field centers are rounded literature approximations (arcminute-level), not survey-pipeline-grade astrometric centers; adequate for selecting nside=128 pixels (~27 arcmin) but not for sub-pixel positioning.

regions.description: Narrow Galactic-longitude band straddling the l=0/360 deg wraparound seam (l in [355, 5] deg), independent of latitude. Exercises longitude-wrap handling in both this validation engine and the candidate map's own pixel indexing.

Top decile (90th-100th percentile) of pixels by the candidate map's own admitted-source count. A reproducible, data-driven proxy for stellar crowding, recomputed fresh from whichever candidate map is supplied to `run` rather than a frozen pixel list.

Union of small fields around well-documented dense dark nebulae / molecular clouds (Coalsack, Pipe Nebula, Ophiuchus dark cloud, Taurus molecular cloud) used in the literature as high-extinction sightlines.
regions.limitation: This is a Galactic-coordinate proxy for known high-extinction dark clouds, not a per-pixel extinction map. The candidate map and this engine currently expose no per-pixel extinction statistic; replace with a `PixelStatPercentile` selector (or an equivalent formula) once one is available.

regions.description: Union of small fields around a handful of the brightest stars on the sky (Sirius, Canopus, Vega), used to check candidate-map and validation behavior near sources that dominate local photon counts and are the most likely to be affected by saturation, masking, or exclusion-rule edge cases.
regions.limitation: Star coordinates are rounded to 0.1 deg from standard catalogue positions and are meant to select the surrounding nside=128 pixel neighborhood, not to pinpoint an exact source pixel.

regions.description: Extreme top percentile (99th-100th) of pixels by the candidate map's own admitted-source count: the most stellar-dense individual pixels in the map, a stricter subset of `dense` used to check whether tolerance failures concentrate in a small number of pathological pixels.
regions.limitation: By construction this region is always a subset of `dense`; the two are expected to overlap and are reported separately to distinguish broad crowding effects from extreme single-pixel outliers.
